cannot_reproduce: Gravity: 1/6 g (1.62 m/s²) — no terrestrial equivalent
Atmosphere: vacuum (~10⁻¹⁰ Pa); no convection, no acoustic hazards from wind
Radiation: unfiltered solar energetic particles and galactic cosmic rays
Absolute temperatures: 40 K in permanently shadowed regions to ~400 K at equatorial noon — far outside any Earth surface range
14-Earth-day continuous daylight / 14-Earth-day darkness cycle — no terrestrial analog

Solar elevation regime: lunar obliquity ~1.54° means the sun never rises above ~6° at the south pole all year. Earth's annual maximum solar elevation cannot drop below ~23.4° (South Pole at summer solstice). No Earth cell can replicate the near-horizon sun regime of the lunar south pole.
Regolith: electrostatic, sharp-edged (no weathering) — no terrestrial surface-level equivalent

slope.source: LOLA LDEM Marius Hills region — mare basalt plains; regional slope typically 1–3°. UNVERIFIED.
slope.notes: UNVERIFIED. Surrounding terrain is flat mare basalt; pit rim may have higher local slope.

roughness.source: LOLA LDEM Marius Hills mare basalt — typical roughness 10–15 m in mare terrain. Paige et al. 2010 supplementary. UNVERIFIED.

local_relief.source: LOLA LDEM Marius Hills — mare basalt plains with low regional relief; volcanic domes in region. 100–400 m within 12 km. UNVERIFIED.

temp_annual_mean.source: Diviner DLRE global equatorial/mid-latitude — equatorial annual mean ~220–260 K. Paige et al. 2010. UNVERIFIED.
temp_annual_mean.basis: APPROXIMATE — to be computed by assemble script.

temp_annual_range.source: Diviner DLRE — equatorial diurnal/annual range ~150–280 K for mare terrain at 14°N. Paige et al. 2010. UNVERIFIED.
temp_annual_range.basis: APPROXIMATE — to be computed by assemble script.

temp_diurnal_range.source: Diviner — equatorial mare: very large diurnal range due to 14-day day/night cycle; ~100–300 K typical. Paige et al. 2010. UNVERIFIED.
temp_diurnal_range.notes: UNVERIFIED. Extreme diurnal range is a key cannot_reproduce item.
temp_diurnal_range.basis: APPROXIMATE — to be computed by assemble script.

illumination_fraction.source: Equatorial location (~14°N): half-year sun / half-year dark per 29.5-day lunar cycle. Computed from orbital geometry. UNVERIFIED.
illumination_fraction.notes: UNVERIFIED. Equatorial illumination fraction ~0.50 (14-day day, 14-day night).

solar_elevation_range.source: Lunar geometry at 14°N: max elevation ~90°−14°+1.54° ≈ 77.5°; moon's obliquity is 1.54°. Noda et al. 2008. UNVERIFIED.

illumination.basis: APPROXIMATE — to be computed by assemble script.

reflectance.source: LROC WAC global mosaic — Marius Hills mare basalt; mare reflectance typically 0.08–0.12 at 604 nm. Scholten et al. 2012. UNVERIFIED.

aridity.basis: REQUIREMENT — maximally arid by definition; no liquid water

ice_polar.notes: Marius Hills Pit is at 14°N — no ground ice expected at equatorial latitude. LEND and SWIM do not indicate ice at this location. ice_polar characteristic not applicable.

geologic_unit.class_description: Imbrian-age mare basalt (unit Im) — volcanic flood basalt plains in Marius Hills region; associated with volcanic domes and pit skylights.
geologic_unit.source: USGS Unified Geologic Map of the Moon v2 — Fortezzo et al. 2020. UNVERIFIED.

pit_location.source: LROC NAC imagery — Wagner & Robinson 2015 (doi:10.1016/j.icarus.2015.09.001); LROC Lunar Pit Atlas. UNVERIFIED at PDS archive.
pit_location.notes: UNVERIFIED. Pit dimensions from Wagner & Robinson 2015 Table 1 (approximate: diameter ~65 m, depth ~35 m — values from published figure; exact values in PDS NAC product). Interpreted as probable lava-tube skylight based on floor morphology and location in Marius Hills volcanic complex.
